'''Richard Stanley Williams''' (born 1951) is an American [[research scientist]] in the field of [[nanotechnology]] and a [[Senior Fellow]] and the founding director of the [[Quantum Science Research Laboratory]] at [[Hewlett-Packard]]. He has over 57 patents, with 40 more patents pending.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chem.ucla.edu/dept/alumni/Seaborg/2007_SEABORG/Williams_bio.html|publisher=[[UCLA]]|title=R. Stanley Williams, Hewlett-Packard Laboratories "Making and Using Functional Nanostructures 2007 Seaborg Symposium"|date=September 2007}}</ref> At HP, he led a group that developed a working [[solid state (electronics)|solid state]] version of [[Leon Chua]]'s [[memristor]].<ref name="Addee2008_05">{{cite web|url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/the-mysterious-memristor|title=The Mysterious Memristor|author=Sally Addee|date=May 2008|publisher=[[IEEE Spectrum]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eetimes.com/showArticle.jhtml?articleID=207403521|title= 'Missing link' memristor created: Rewrite the textbooks?|author=R. Colin Johnson|publisher=[[EE Times]]|date=2008-04-30}}</ref>

Williams earned a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[chemical physics]] in 1974 from [[Rice University]] and a [[Ph.D.]] in [[physical chemistry]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1978. After graduating, he worked at [[Bell Labs]] before joining the faculty at [[UCLA]], where he served as a professor from 1980 to 1995. He then joined [[HP Labs]] as director of its [[Information and Quantum Systems Lab]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hpl.hp.com/about/bios/stanwilliams.html|publisher=Hewlett-Packard|title=Biography|access-date=2010-09-03|archive-date=2008-05-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513192702/http://www.hpl.hp.com/about/bios/stanwilliams.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* [[Foresight Institute Feynman Prize in Nanotechnology]] (2000)
* [[Herman Bloch Medal]] for Industrial Research (2004)
* [[Springer Science+Business Media|Julius Springer]] Prize for Applied Physics (2000)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/physics/optics/journal/340?detailsPage=contentItemPage&CIPageCounter=104813#anchor3|publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media]]|title=Julius Springer Prize for Applied Physics}}</ref>
* [[Glenn T. Seaborg Medal]], UCLA (2007)
